answer: The karst cap is enforced at intake and voyage shows the per-origin counts. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a trellis tag. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a swarm in one epoch however much capital it holds, since each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
